articleTitle: sentiment analysis on massive open online course evaluation
abstract: Massive open online courses (MOOCs) are ever-increasing for their significant and open learning content to participants. So far, however, there has been little discussion on how to evaluate effectively the experience of participants in a MOOC. Meanwhile, sentiment analysis (SA) becomes a hot area in decision-making and spreads across many fields such as internet media monitoring, product service improvement and marketing. A wide gap still exists between SA and education research. From the view of SA, this study samples 725 clean annotated reviews from China University MOOC website and preprocesses them for further analysis, then explores learner's opinion towards seven aspects about MOOCs with the supervised Naive Bayes classifier. Furthermore, this paper focuses on process evaluation and sheds light on learners' positive or negative opinion towards MOOCs success indicator. Consequently, the results show learners feel great satisfaction with course instructor, interaction and course content, while they express their dissatisfaction with course assessment and learning platform health. This study also indicates SA is applicable to education research and can be incorporated into online learning systems which contributes to realize the real-time analysis of student feedback.

articleTitle: Detection of Stealthy Cyber-attack in Distributed DC Microgrids Based on LSTM Neural Network
abstract: Distributed DC microgrids, which mainly consist of cyber layer and physical layer, can be classified as a classical cyber-physical system. Compared with the physical layer, the cyber layer has a significant risk of malicious cyber-attack due to its inherent vulnerability. This paper investigates a lightweight cyber-attack detection problem for distributed DC microgrids with bounded process and measurement noises. More precisely, the cyber-attack under consideration is assumed to be the stealthy cyber-attack. A long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network-based strategy is proposed to construct the attack detection scheme without using the information of the noises. Case studies indicate that the proposed attack detection strategy can work effectively in the following two cases: i) the statistical characteristics of system noises are unknown; ii) the magnitude of the cyber-attack is lightweight, which is detected extremely hard by traditional detectors such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi^{2}$</tex> detector.

articleTitle: Anti-synchronization of Multi-Weighted Coupled Complex-Valued Delayed Memristive Neural Networks with Coupling Delays
abstract: This paper studies anti-synchronization of multi-weighted coupled complex-valued delayed memristive neural networks (MWCCVDMNNs) with coupling delays. We derive a criterion for guaranteeing anti-synchronization of MWCCVDMNNs with coupling delays, by means of Lyapunov functional method and designing an appropriate controller. Moreover, a numerical example is given to verify the correctness of the obtained theoretical result.

articleTitle: Finite-time Synchronization of Fractional-order Delayed Memristive Neural Networks by Discontinuous Control Scheme
abstract: In this paper, the problem of the finite-time synchronization is investigated about a class of fractional-order delayed memristive neural networks (FDMNNs). Under the framework of Filippov solution, a discontinuous feedback controller is designed to achieve finite-time synchronization of such systems. In addition, the upper limit of synchronization time is estimated by fractional-order differential inequality. Finally, a numerical example is given to show the correctness of the conclusion.

articleTitle: Anti-Synchronization Control of Fuzzy Inertial Neural Networks with Distributed Time Delays
abstract: This paper investigates the global anti-synchronization control for a class of fuzzy inertial neural networks(FINNs) with distributed time delays. By using Lyapunov stability theory and some inequality techniques, some new results are derived to get global anti-synchronization of the investigated FINNs. The systems considered in this paper are with inertial terms and fuzzy terms, which are more general and meaningful. And we get the global anti-synchronization results directly from the FINNs themselves without the reduced-order method. At last, illustrative examples are given to show the effectiveness of the results.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Synchronization of Inertial Memristive Neural Networks
abstract: This article investigates the predefined-time synchronization (PTS) of inertial memristive neural networks (IMNNs). First, we reduce the order of the system and design an effective controller for the error system. Furthermore, several new criteria for PTS of IMNNs are obtained and a user-defined settling time is provided. Lastly, the effectiveness of the results is proved by simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Time Series of Landslide Displacement Prediction based on VMD-LSTM
abstract: This paper proposes a new model Variational Mode Decomposition-Long-Short Term Memory(VMD-LSTM) for landslide displacement prediction. Firstly, Variational Mode Decomposition(VMD) decomposes the landslide displacement time series into multiple intrinsic mode functions(IMFs) to reduce the interference of noise. At the same time, three normalization methods process the data to explore the applicability of normalization method to model. Then, each decomposed IMF is predicted by LSTM model. Finally, the prediction result of each IMF is added to obtain the final predicted value. In this paper, the landslide displacement sequence of Baishuihe in the Three Gorges Reservoir area is taken as one case. This experiment proved the feasibility of VMD-LSTM model. Comparing with the traditional LSTM moel, the root-mean-squareerror(RMSE) of VMD-LSTM is reduced to 9.75.

articleTitle: Memristor-Based Neural Network Circuit of Long-term Memory
abstract: As an important part of memory, memristor-based neural networks of memory are seldom involved in long-term memory. In this paper, a memristor-based neural network of long-term memory is designed. The designed circuit consists of a synapse module and a voltage adjustment module. The functions such as learning, forgetting, long-term memory and self-protection are implemented by the circuit. When a neuron forms a long-term memory for a stimulus, it responds more quickly to the same stimulus again. The research of long-term memory is helpful for neural network to simulate more real brain memory. The neural network circuit of long-term memory provides a reference for the further development of brain-like systems.

articleTitle: Impulsive Consensus Algorithms for Second-order Multi-agent Formation Based on the Improved Artificial Potential Field
abstract: In this paper, the impulsive consensus problem for second-order multi-agent formation based on the improved artificial potential field (APF) is investigated. In order to control the agent, the motion model of the Mecanum wheel trolley is established. In order to realize the consensus of multi-agent system, a second-order impulsive model is used to control the formation. To avoid collisions during formation establishment, the improved APF method is introduced and applied, and the repulsive force field and attractive field potential function are improved to solve the local minimum value and target unreachable problems of APF. Finally, the simulation and experiment show the effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: A Read and Write Method for Forgetting Memristor Crossbar Array with Long-term and Short-term Memory
abstract: In this paper, time slot technology is designed based on the single forgetting memristor synapse with single voltage source to read and write the forgetting memristor crossbar array. The amplitude of the voltage source signal is used to set the corresponding long-term and short-term memory weights, and the circuit protection signal is used to improve the security of the nanoscale memristor crossbar array. By analyzing the forgetting properties of memristor synapses, the forgetting memristor crossbar array with long-term memory, short-term memory (LSM) and its corresponding read-write mode are demonstrated. Because the forgetting memristor crossbar array can store both long-term and short-term memories, the application of forgetting memristor crossbar array to image storage can show the spontaneous evolution of images.

articleTitle: Chaotic Time Series Prediction using Three-Dimensional FOA and Echo State Network
abstract: Chaotic time series prediction is critical in the fields of artificial intelligence. Recently, the Echo State Network (ESN) with nonlinear computing capability has been widely used to perform time series prediction tasks. However, the parameters of ESN are needed to vary to application scenarios and are usually set by human experience, which affects the performance of ESN. In this work, the Three-Dimensional Fruit Fly Optimization Algorithm is proposed to optimize the parameters of ESN (TDFOA-ESN) by adding swarm collaboration and random perturbation. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by using benchmark datasets (NARMA and Mackey-Glass) and real-world time series (Beijing PM2.5 Data). In addition, the root mean squared error, normal root mean squared error and determination coefficient are used to evaluate the performance of TDFOA-ESN model. The experiment shows that the normal root mean squared error is reduced by 80.85% compared with other approaches. Therefore, the proposed TDFOA-ESN model provides a beneficial alternative for the time series prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Finite-time synchronization of complex-valued neural networks with adaptive coupling weights
abstract: The finite-time synchronization problem is considered for the networked complex-valued neural networks in the present paper. Different from the separating method in the literature, the complex-valued state variables are used directly to design finite-time control scheme, involving impulsive control and two-phase method. By employing adaptive laws, the finite-time synchronization criterion are given in terms of algebraic inequalities. Based on the two-phase method, a novel piecewise control scheme is proposed, in order to simplify the control design. A numerical example is given to show the validity of the proposed control.

articleTitle: Leader-following Consensus of Fractional-order Multi-agent Systems with Feedback Control Protocol
abstract: This paper investigates the leader-following consensus of fractional-order multi-agent systems by designing a novel feedback control protocol. Based on Laplace transform, Nyquist stability criterion and stability theory of fractional-order systems, some sufficient conditions are obtained to realize leader-following consensus. Finally, a numerical example is given to illustrate the main results.

articleTitle: An inertial neuro-dynamic system for solving zero-one integer programming
abstract: This paper presents an inertial neuro-dynamic system to solve zero-one integer programming. We transform the problem of zero-one integer programming into a relatively easy problem only subject to linear equality constraints by using a nonlinear complementarity problem function. Subsequently, a inertial neuro-dynamic system is proposed to solve above transformed problem. It is shown that the proposed inertial neuro-dynamic system is stable and the equilibrium point converges to optimal solution set. It is worth emphasizing that our developed inertial neuro-dynamic system achieves faster convergence speed and explores more optimal solutions in a fixed initial value by adjusting the inertial factor. Finally, according to the experimental results on two illustrative examples, the proposed method is highly effective.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation of fractional-order memristor-based chaotic systems using state transition algorithm
abstract: Parameter estimation of fractional-order memristor-based chaotic systems is very important. In this study, the state transition algorithm (STA) is used to estimate the parameters of the fractional-order memristor-based chaotic systems. The performance of the proposed method is comprehensively evaluated on two typical fractional-order memristor-based chaotic systems. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Multi-modal Emotion Recognition Network Based on Multi-task Learning
abstract: Human emotion recognition is a very important part of the human-computer interaction process, and its application scenarios are very wide, which has received more and more attention in recent years. In this paper, a lightweight multimodal emotion recognition network is proposed, which makes the network model as small as possible under the premise of ensuring network accuracy, so that human emotion recognition can be well applied to mobile devices. Specifically, this article uses three modalities: audio, video, and text as input data. The audio signal is converted into MFCC and video signal using MobileNet for feature extraction, thereby reducing the amount of network parameters. For text data, Bert is used for feature extraction, and features extracted from the three modalities are combined through the attention mechanism. Finally, in order to improve the recognition rate and generalization ability of the network, a multi-task structure is also introduced. The experimental results show that the lightweight model can effectively reduce the amount of network parameters, greatly reduce the requirements for equipment, and make it possible to apply emotion recognition on the mobile terminal.

articleTitle: A class of offset boostable 3-D memristive system
abstract: Offset boosting of a chaotic signal is the key issue for chaos production. Memristor is a new nonlinear component that promotes chaotic oscillator design for its integrated memory dynamics. By memristor introducing variable boostable dynamical flows can be upgraded to be offset boostable memristive chaotic systems. Following this routine, a memristor can be planted into a dynamical flow by direct introducing, cross term matching, feedback augment, and internal variable transferring. Easy offset boosting is discussed and demonstrated by linearly shifted average values under a unified set of Lyapunov exponents. However, if the boostable system variable is regarded as the internal variable of a memristor, offset boosting with this dimension becomes not necessary for the corresponding system but leaves a shortcut for offset boosting if the system is upgraded with dimension.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Memristor Neural Networks with State-Dependent Delay
abstract: The processing of neural information involves multilevel and multi-region coupling and cooperation. Therefore, the neural activity of structural neural network is worth studying and discussing from the perspective of model and evolution. This article establishes a memristor neural network model with state-dependent delay for the first time. Then, some sufficient algebraic criteria for the local exponential stability of such memristor neural networks are given by pure analysis method. In addition, a numerical example is given to verify the effectiveness of the criteria.

articleTitle: Bipolar Pulse-induced Coexisting Symmetric Attractors in Hopfield Neural Network
abstract: By exerting a bipolar pulse (BP) current on one neuron, a non-autonomous Hopfield neural network (HNN) model is proposed in this paper, where complex dynamical effects of coexisting symmetric attractors are exhibited apparently. Firstly, using graphical method to calculate the switchable equilibrium points, we find that unstable node-focus (UNF) and stable node-focus (SNF) are existed in the model. Additionally, using multiple dynamical methods to reveal the initial-related bistable patterns, we find that the proposed model behaves coexisting symmetric attractors. Finally, we develop an electronic neuron circuit for the model on the analog level, and the PSIM-based circuit simulations excellently verify the numerical results.

articleTitle: Uniform Stability of Fractional-order Memristive Neural Networks with Hybrid Time-Varying Delays
abstract: This article discusses the uniform stability of Caputo fractional-order memristive neural networks (FMNNs) with discrete delay and distributed delay. By virtue of fractional-order Razumikhin-type theorem, interval matrix method, differential inclusion and set-valued mapping, a LMI-based standard is acquired to certify uniform stability of the addressed FMNNs. Lastly, the validity of the constructed criterion is manifested by an example.

articleTitle: Memristor-based Brain-like Reconfigurable Neuromorphic System
abstract: It improves the data processing performance and efficiency notably that the memristor-based neuromorphic system is constructed by mimicking the features of brain. This paper proposes a memristor-based circuit implementation for brain-like reconfigurable neuromorphic system. This neuromorphic system contains memristor-based back-propagation neural network, memristor-based long short-term memory network, and memristor-based associative memory network. The reconfigurable circuit components can constitute the circuit hardware of the three memristor-based networks according to the task requirements or release the circuit hardware of the three memristor-based networks based on the forgetting mechanism along with time of the biology. Hence, this neuromorphic system has dynamic topology structure, which is similar as the feature of biological neural networks. A case study of the memristor-based brain-like reconfigurable neuromorphic system is presented in the paper. In the case study, the memristor-based back-propagation neural network and the memristor-based long short-term memory network are applied for the image recognition and speech recognition, respectively. The recognition results of the two memristor-based networks are input to the memristor-based associative memory network to recall the correlated information. This neuromorphic system has the potential to apply for the intelligent robot system.

articleTitle: Multistability of Memristor-Based Impulsive Neural Networks With Time-Varying Delays
abstract: This paper investigates multistability of memristor-based impulsive neural networks with time-varying delays. By using the state space partition method and Lyapunov functions, a sufficient condition is obtained to ensure there are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2K+1)^{n}$</tex> equilibrium points coexist in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> neurons networks, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is a parameter concerned with the activation function, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(K+1)^{n}$</tex> of them are locally stable. At the end of this paper, the conclusions are further summarized.

articleTitle: Multiple $\psi$-Type Stability of High-Order Neural Networks With Unbounded Time-Varying Delays
abstract: This paper mainly explores dynamical behaviors of high-order neural networks with unbounded time-varying delays. Based on inequality techniques, decomposition of state space and fixed point principle, some sufficient criteria are proposed to ensure that there exist <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\prod\nolimits_{i=1}^{n}(2R_{i}+1)$</tex> equilibrium points in high-order neural networks. After that, by choosing appropriate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi$</tex>-type functions, it reveals that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\prod\nolimits_{i=1}^{n}(R_{i}+1)$</tex> equilibrium points are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi$</tex>-type stable and the convergence rate can be further estimated. The derived conclusions contain and extend the previous results.

articleTitle: Synchronization and Adaptive Control for Coupled Fractional-Order Reaction-Diffusion Neural Networks with Multiple Weights
abstract: In this paper, a type of coupled fractional-order reaction-diffusion neural networks (CFORDNNs) with multiple weights is presented. By utilizing Laplace inverse transform and some inequality techniques, a sufficient condition is given to make sure the proposed network model is synchronized. On the other hand, in order to guarantee the synchronization of the network model, an appropriate adaptive control strategy is also developed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive control scheme is substantiated by employing a numerical example and its simulation results.

articleTitle: Fixed-time Stabilization of Delayed Neural Networks: A Switching Control Framework Design
abstract: In this paper, the fixed-time stabilization for a type of nonlinear delayed neural networks (DNNS) is investigated. By designing an appropriate switching closed-loop controller and using inequality techniques, a sufficient condition is developed to guarantee the fixed-time stabilization. Finally, two simulation examples are provided to demonstrate the validity of our theoretical results.

articleTitle: On Controllability of Transportation Networks with Fractional-Order Dynamics
abstract: This paper adopt the fractional derivative approach to formulate the fractional-order transportation networks, which considers the propagation dynamics and the users' behaviors in terms of route choices. We then investigate the controllability of the fractional-order transportation networks by employing the PBH rank condition and the QR. The problem of controller position and number in fractional-order transportation networks is solved. Finally, we illustrate two numerical examples vaslidate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Carbon-Aware Economic Dispatch: A Singular Perturbation Approach
abstract: With the worsen of environmental problems, the carbon emission of the energy system has quickly become the spotlight. However, Most of the existing works focus on the economic dispatch without carbon emission constraints. In this paper, we focus on the economic dispatch with carbon emission constraints. First, a novel mathematical model which characterizes the economic dispatch with carbon emission constraints is given. Then it is followed by the distributed carbon-aware dispatch strategy design based on the singular perturbation system.

articleTitle: Real-Time Power System State Estimation
abstract: Power system state estimation (PSSE) is one of the most important functions in power system operation and control. A key challenge for precise PSSE is the inherent nonlinearity of measurements with respect to system states. In this paper, the convex relaxation method is used for removing the nonlinearity in the PSSE problem. Moreover, the alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) is utilized for addressing the real-time PSSE problem. In addition, the vectorization operator are developed for solving the quadratic matrix equation and accelerating the ADMM. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of our method are verified via a benchmark case on IEEE 14-bus system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Command Filtering Control for Nonlinear MIMO State Constraints Systems
abstract: In this paper, a command-filter-based adaptive fuzzy control strategy is proposed for a class of nonlinear multiple input and multiple output(MIMO) systems with full state constraints. The appropriate barrier Lyapunov function is employed to prevent the constraints violation, and the command-filtered backstepping control method is proposed to remove the explosion of differentiation and lessen the computational burden. In addition, fuzzy logic system is employed to approximate the unknown nonlinear function, and the proposed compensating signals can make up for the error caused by the command filters. The proposed control strategy guarantees that all signals in the closed-loop system are semiglobal uniformly ultimately bounded by adjusting those designed system parameters. The simulation result is introduced to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Pinning Synchronization of Multi-weighted Coupled Neural Networks without and with Time Delays
abstract: This paper solves event-triggered pinning synchronization problem for multi-weighted coupled neural networks (MWCNNs) without and with time delays. On one side, by designing appropriate event-triggered controller, a pinning synchronization criterion for MWCNNs under the designed event-triggered condition are derived based on the Lyapunov functional method and some inequality techniques. On the other side, we also investigate the event-triggered pinning synchronization of multi-weighted coupled delayed neural networks (MWCDNNs) and eatablish a corresponding synchronization criterion based on the suitable event-triggered pinning controller and condition. Finally, an example with numerical simulation results is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained theoretical results.

articleTitle: Fixed-time Formation Control for Second-order Multi-agent Systems with Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the fixed-time formation control problem for second-order multi-agent system, where disturbance may exist in the dynamics of each agent. A fixed-time formation control protocol is proposed and the convergence time is calculated. Finally, a numerical example is presented to validate the theoretical result.

articleTitle: Memristive Network-based Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores the relation between Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm and memristive network. There are some relations between swarm intelligence and memristive network. Inspired by the correlation between colony optimization and memristive network, mapping rules between AFSA's 4 main behaviors and memristive network has highlighted in this paper. In this paper the motion of single fish is first simulated, then the motion of more fish is simulated. Finally, we make comparison of the trend of motion fish swarm and concept model.

articleTitle: Appointed-weight Privacy-preserving Consensus of Multi-agent Systems
abstract: Though privacy-preserving consensus of multi-agent systems has been extensively studied, one issue remains unsolved. That is, the final consensus value may not be exactly the average of all the agents' initial values. In this paper, we investigate the privacy-preserving consensus problem of multiagent systems, where the final consensus value is the weighted average of all the agents' initial values with predefined weights. A noise generation mechanism is designed, and a novel privacy-preserving consensus algorithm is proposed. Theoretical analysis shows that the proposed algorithm can realize appointed-weight consensus while achieving privacy preserving.

articleTitle: Saturation region attractivity analysis for memristive neural networks under the strong external input
abstract: Memristive neural networks are recurrent neural networks with memristors as connection weights. Such n dimensional neural networks can be seen as a family of 2n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>sub networks. By math analysis method, we discuss saturation region attractivity of such neural networks. Then we present one sufficient condition for networks saturation region attractivity with the strong external input. At last, one examples is given for verify our results.

articleTitle: Exponential Stability of Stochastic Dynamic Memristor Delayed Cellular Neural Networks in the Flux-Charge Domain
abstract: Throughout this paper, the global stability of the dynamic memristor(DM)-delayed cellular neural networks(DCNNs) in stochastic phenomenon is studied, according to the flux-charge analytical method. By utilizing the stochastic analysis technique and constructing the proper Lyapunov functions, some sufficient criteria are proposed to obtain the exponential stability of the stochastic DM-DCNNs in flux-charge domain.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Neuro-adaptive Containment of Multiagent Systems with Directed Topology
abstract: This paper studies the fully distributed containment problem for multiagent systems (MASs) with multiple leaders and uncertain dynamics under detail balanced directed topology, where the leaders are subject to some unknown control inputs. By using the neural network (NN) approximation technique, a discontinuous controller together with adaptive coupling law and adaptive NN law is proposed. And it is shown that the asymptotically fully distributed containment can be achieved even if the upper bounds of the leaders' nonzero inputs and the NN approximation error are unknown. Finally, simulations are given to validate the theoretical result.

articleTitle: Fixed-/Preassigned-Time Stabilization of Memristive Neural Networks with Discontinuous Activations
abstract: In this paper, the fixed-time stabilization (FTS) and preassigned-time stabilization (PTS) problems for memristive neural networks (MNNs) with discontinuous activation functions (DAF) is investigated by designing a unified controller. In addition, less conservative stabilization criteria are derived to ensure the FTS and PTS of MNNs. Besides, a more accurate estimate of settling time is obtained based on Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, a numerical simulation is illustrated to verify the validity of theoretical results.

articleTitle: Finite-time synchronization of memristive neural networks via quantized intermittent control
abstract: This paper focuses on finite-time synchronization (FTS) based on quantized intermittent control of memristive neural networks (MNN). The synchronization of the system constructed under the concept of Filippov solution is achieved by the design of a new quantized intermittent controller (QIC). The corresponding conditions for achieving system synchronization are established based on FTS theory and intermittent strategies. Finally, a numerical simulation is given to verify the correctness of the theory.

articleTitle: Modeling and Gait Planning Simulation of Tower-Climbing Robot Based on ROS
abstract: In order to improve the automation level of the power system, reduce the labor intensity of electric workers in the maintenance of the high-voltage power transmission system, and ensure their personal safety. With reference to the climbing gait of the inchworm, a multi-joint angle Tower-climbing robot was designed and proposed. The development of climbing robots is a relatively innovative scientific field. Taking into account the intuitiveness and high efficiency of the robot development process, the robot development method based on ROS (Robot Operating System) is adopted, and kinematic analysis and solution configuration are carried out. Firstly, the kinematics modeling of the climbing robot is carried out to solve the robot kinematics problem. Then the trajectory planning method based on Cartesian space is used to plan the trajectory of the end of the climbing robot, and it is simulated and verified by Matlab. Finally, the climbing robot model file is imported into ROS, and the gait planning control program of the quadruped robot is written through the user API to simulate the motion planning. At the same time, RVIZ can visualize the robot's movement process and obtain other relevant data during the movement, indicating the correctness of the trajectory planning. The results show that the development method of climbing robot based on ROS is feasible.

articleTitle: Memristor-based Echo State Network and Prediction for Time Series
abstract: This paper proposes echo state network based on the memristor and applies it to the prediction of chaotic time series. The memristor is used to replace the connection synapses between neurons in the echo state network reservoir, which improves the prediction performance of the network. A simulation experiment is carried out on the echo state network based on the memristor in the widely used chaotic time series prediction. The experiment results show that the echo state network based on the memristor improves the prediction accuracy and performance of the network.

articleTitle: A Study on Calculating and Counting the Low-cost Paths in Bus Transportation Networks
abstract: Multiple low-cost paths may exist between two stops in a bus transportation network (BTN). In most previous studies, only the lowest-cost paths were considered. By fully taking account of all these paths, more accurate and effective results of BTN researches may be established. In this paper, we present a preliminary study on calculating and counting the low-cost paths in a BTN. Specifically, we present an algorithm of calculating the low-cost paths between two arbitrary stops in BTNs, which takes account of both the bus riding edges and short-distance walking edges. Besides, a case study based on the BTN of Hangzhou in China of analyzing the number of the low-cost paths with transfer times less than 3 is given. Results show that the number of the low-cost paths between two stops increases exponentially with passengers' tolerance degree to the travel cost, and the number is sensitive to the factors of transfer-times and walking distance.

articleTitle: Fundus Disease Image Classification based on Improved Transformer
abstract: In recent years, the progress of deep learning and fundus camera technology makes it possible to diagnose fundus diseases by computer. However, the fundus image dataset is relatively small, which makes the pure transformer model challenging to be applied to medical disease analysis. Therefore, this paper proposes a Transformer Eye (TransEye) fine-grained fundus disease image classification method based on the self-attention mechanism to assist diagnosis. TransEye combines the advantages of Convolution Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer model. It can not only effectively extract the underlying features, but also establish the remote dependence of the image. So, it can locate the most discriminative image area and complete end-to-end training. Evaluated the classification effect of our method on the preprocessed OIA dataset, the experimental results show the superiority of TransEye.

articleTitle: Digital Hardware Implementation of Optimized Spiking Neurons
abstract: Neuromorphic computing and spiking neural networks have seen growing attention lately, especially in combination with event-based sensors and in robotics. To deploy such spiking neural networks, suitable hardware platforms are required. Neuromorphic hardware can be built based on various neuron models. However, only few publications so far investigate which neuron models are best suited for hardware implementation and many platforms use simple models like leaky integrate-and-fire. This work investigates how various neuron models can be implemented in hardware, applying different optimization and approximation techniques. The optimized neurons are prototyped on a field-programmable gate array and compared based on hardware resource requirements, power consumption and accuracy versus non-optimized models. Promising candidates for hardware implementation are pointed out and different metrics are evaluated, providing a guideline to trade-off the hardware implementation and performance for different neuron types.

articleTitle: Learning Through Structure: Towards Deep Neuromorphic Knowledge Graph Embeddings
abstract: Computing latent representations for graph-structured data is an ubiquitous learning task in many industrial and academic applications ranging from molecule synthetization to social network analysis and recommender systems. Knowledge graphs are among the most popular and widely used data representations related to the Semantic Web. Next to structuring factual knowledge in a machine-readable format, knowledge graphs serve as the backbone of many artificial intelligence applications and allow the ingestion of context information into various learning algorithms. Graph neural networks attempt to encode graph structures in low-dimensional vector spaces via a message passing heuristic between neighboring nodes. Over the recent years, a multitude of different graph neural network architectures demonstrated ground-breaking performances in many learning tasks. In this work, we propose a strategy to map deep graph learning architectures for knowledge graph reasoning to neuromorphic architectures. Based on the insight that randomly initialized and untrained (i.e., frozen) graph neural networks are able to preserve local graph structures, we compose a frozen neural network with shallow knowledge graph embedding models. We experimentally show that already on conventional computing hardware, this leads to a significant speedup and memory reduction while maintaining a competitive performance level. Moreover, we extend the frozen architecture to spiking neural networks, introducing a novel, event-based and highly sparse knowledge graph embedding algorithm that is suitable for implementation in neuromorphic hardware.

articleTitle: An image classification method based on Echo State Network
abstract: As a traditional neural network architecture, Echo State Network(ESN) has achieved good results in time series forecasting. However, in the past ten years, few people have conducted research on its application to images, especially in classification tasks. Echo State Network is a kind of Recurrent Neural Network, it has the advantages of simple structure and convenient training. It only needs to train its output weight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w_{out}$</tex>, which saves a lot of time and resources. In this article, we input the whole picture into ESN in multi-input mode to classify images, and use the traditional Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) model to compare experiments with it, and the results found that esn has better stability and accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on a New Type of Chaotic Image Encryption Algorithm Combining DNA Operation and S-box
abstract: Given the fixed DNA coding and operation rules of DNA coding, the single S-box operation function cannot meet the more complex and secure encryption requirements. Therefore, a new type of complex symmetric chaotic image encryption combining DNA up and down cyclic shift operation and S-box operation is the proposed algorithm. In this way, we propose a new chaotic map. The encryption system combines the sensitivity and unpredictability of the chaotic system to the initial value to generate random sequences and S-boxes It replaces the sequence matrix with S-box to further increase the randomness. Finally, the replaced matrix and the original image are DNA-encoded and combined with the proposed new calculation to complete the encryption operation. The algorithm proposed in this paper is more secure and robust through simulation experiments and performance index analysis.

articleTitle: Block-Clustering on Neural Networks for Large-scale Memristor-based Implementation
abstract: The emergence of memristors with tunable resistance states provides building blocks for neuromorphic computing systems (NCSs) as electric synapses. However, the large-scale realization of memristive neural networks confronts with challenges, that is, a rapid increase in network complexity causes high-cost mapping and low-reliability of memristor connections. The general method is to make neural networks sparse. But most sparse networks actually reduce the utilization rate of the memristors and the expected large scale is normally beyond that can be offered by current integration technology of memristors. In this paper, a reliable block-clustering framework (BCF) with universality is proposed for both directed and undirected memristive neural networks. The idea of sparse and block clustering can realize the use of fewer memristor integrated circuits, and solve the current problem of difficult large-scale integration of memristive arrays. BCF integrates block clustering approaches and memristor array properties to cluster original large sparse synapse connections into several smaller and denser groups as much as possible. Then, the denser connections can be realized by memristor crossbar arrays with enhanced utilization rate and the small number of intra-group connections can be realized by discrete memristor synapses. BCF consists of iterative spectral clustering (ISC), swap clustering (SC) and hybrid ISC+SC, where these three methods are evaluated according to the criteria including outlier percentage, time consumption. Experiment results and analysis demonstrate that BCF can be effectively used on neural networks with different sparsities. This novel clustering framework provides a promising key technique for improving the utilization of memristor crossbar array and guaranteeing the communication quality of the whole system, which is conductive to promote large scale NCSs implementation.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Synchronization Control for Uncertain Complex Networks
abstract: This article concentrates on the predefined-time synchronization problem for uncertain complex networks (CNs) with identical nodes. A predefined-time Lyapunov stability characterization method is firstly proposed, based on which the continuous predefined-time controller is dexterously designed. Besides, some sufficient conditions in the form of linear matrix inequalities are established to guarantee the addressed CN realizing the synchronization within the predefined-time. The predefined-time considered here can be specified in advance according to the actual requirements, which is independent of the system initial conditions, the system parameters, and the other controller parameters. In addition, the network parameter uncertainties, which satisfying the norm bounded constraint, are also taken into account to describe more actual networks. Finally, a numerical example is presented to demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Constant-Stepsize Distributed Optimization Algorithm with Malicious Nodes
abstract: This paper develops a consensus-based distributed (sub)gradient descent algorithm, which has a faster convergence rate in the presence of malicious nodes. To achieve this, two main methods are used in the proposed algorithm. The first is using the local filtering algorithm to counteract the attacks of malicious nodes; The second is using the constant step size in the distributed (sub)gradient descent algorithm rather than diminishing step size to accelerate the convergence rate. As a result, the proposed algorithm improves the convergence rate in the presence of malicious nodes. Finally, a numerical example is presented to verify the proposed algorithm, and the possible future research directions are given.

articleTitle: On Synchronization of Coupled Fractional-Order Neural Networks in Finite-Time Sense
abstract: This paper focuses on the synchronization of coupled fractional-order neural networks with time-varying delays in finite-time sense. By introducing an effective controller, the synchronization of coupled fractional-order neural networks is realized in finite time, and a settling time can be estimated. Moreover, sufficient criteria are deduced to ensure the realization of synchronization in finite-time sense. The results of this paper are general and are also applicable for the synchronization of integer-order neural networks. Finally, a numerical example is provided to verify the correctness and validity of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Cohen-Grossberg neural networks with time-varying delays via state-constraint impulsive controller
abstract: The aim of this paper is to study the synchronization problem of delayed Cohen-Grossberg neural networks with impulse controller, in which the saturation limit of the impulse is taken into account. Firstly, by constructing a suitable Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional candidate and using techniques of inequality and convex analysis, several criteria are obtained to reach the synchronization goal of delayed Cohen-Grossberg neural networks with state-constraint impulsive controller. Based on these criteria, the region of attraction for the synchronization error system is estimated. Secondly, the special case that only part of the states subject from saturation is also considered, and the corresponding results are obtained. Moreover, when Cohen-Grossberg neural networks are simplified to special cases such as Hopfield neural networks, our results have been improved and expanded. Finally, the simulation example shows the effectiveness of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Self-triggered Consensus Control for Multilayered Cluster Network
abstract: This paper studies the multilayered cluster network, and proposes a correlated self-triggered consensus control protocol. An event prediction algorithm is designed to avoid continuous detection. In each cluster, the detection instant is calculated based on the current triggering state, such that each cluster in different layers has its own event detection instants. The algorithm is validated on both a numerical simulation example and a DC microgrid clusters control scheme.

articleTitle: Stability of Inertial Delayed Neural Networks Via Event-Triggered Impulsive Control
abstract: This paper studies the stability of inertial delayed neural networks via event-triggered impulsive control (ETIC), where impulsive instants are determined by an effective Lyapunov-based impulsive event triggered mechanism (IETM). Based on the IETM, the Zeno behavior is excluded and ensures the globally exponential stability and h-stability of the neural networks by constructing Lyapunov function and some different restrictive conditions. In addition, the delay term in inertial neural networks is well dealt with the two lemmas given in this paper. It is shown that inertial delayed neural networks can be stabilized through this event-triggered impulsive control. Finally, two numerical examples and their simulations are carried out to verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Designing a Novel Memristor-based Chaotic System Pumped by Cosine and its Application in Image Encryption
abstract: Memristor, a nonlinear element with nanometer size, can be applied in chaotic system and thus enhancing complexity of the chaotic system. Therefore, a novel memristor-based 4D multi-scroll chaotic system via cosine is successfully designed in this letter. The main feature of this system is that the scroll number are sensitive to initial values, the transient simulation time, the flux variation of memristor and the strength of memristor, which is a significant difference from other chaotic systems reported before. Furthermore, the chaotic characteristics have been declared by using time series, 0-1 test chart, and Poincare maps. Besides, the number of scrolls can be controlled by designing a state feedback controller to select the ideal number of scrolls, and such a method for controlling the scroll number is extremely meaningful in suppressing the nonlinearity of chaotic systems. Finally, an algorithm for image encryption is proposed based on the bitwise and cross-transition between adjacent pixels. Both confusion and diffusion are related to the memristor-based chaotic system. Many statistical tests and security analysis show that this algorithm has a good security performance, which can be compared with other recently proposed image encryption algorithms.

articleTitle: Zero-Hopf bifurcation of a reaction-diffusion memristive BAM neural network with time delay
abstract: In this paper, a reaction-diffusion memristive BAM neural network with time delay is constructed. Then, the zero-Hopf bifurcation conditions are obtained and the third-order normal form of zero-Hopf bifurcation are obtained by using the center manifold theorem and the normal form theory. Through analysing the normal form, the dynamic regions on coupling strength of memristor and time dealy plane are obtained, which has six regions. Some interesting dynamics are found in these areas.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Tobacco Storage Monitoring and Conservation Data Management System
abstract: When under production, after harvest ‚curing and redrying, tobacco lamina also need a mellowing process in the warehouse of not less than 24 months to achieve naturally mellowy, during which certain temperature and humidity is needed. In the traditional management mode, tobacco storage and conservation were mainly managed by manual and ERP systems. It was difficult to display and query data, to statistically analyze data and do risk modeling, and the whole process lacked the supervision of the operation link. A tobacco storage monitoring and maintenance data management system is designed in this paper, through the arrangement of sensors in the warehouse and tobacco stacks, it's able to get the data such as the temperature and humidity of the warehoused, tobacco box temperature, oxygen and so on to monitor the warehouse automatically. By collecting, gathering, analyzing all kinds of data, and accessing to the data models trained by BP neural network to calculate and decide, it not only guide the gas control and maintenance operations, also implement the intelligent management of data. The software function of the system is composed of basic data processing unit, inventory management, monitoring and alarm, data overview and other modules. The system is applied to the storage of the company in different areas of the country, realizing centralized data management, and it has been connected to the National Industrial Internet Identification Analysis Second-Level Node Business Management System. Since its operation for 2 years, it has realized energy saving and emission reduction, and greatly improved the economic benefits of the enterprise.

articleTitle: On Global Asymptotic Stability of Parameter Estimation of Extended Dynamic Regressors with not Persistently Exciting
abstract: In this paper, by fully taking available linearly independent and bounded operators, a sufficient and richness criterion similar to the condition of persistent excitation in continuous systems of frequency is proposed for dynamic regressors extension and mixing(DREM) estimators. With the excitation input is sufficiently rich of order 2n, asymptotically convergence for DREM procedure could be guaranteed. Also, the effectiveness of the transfer function operators is explored, a more efficient method of selecting operational factors is proposed for better performance. At last, some numerical examples are offered to show the simulation effect.

articleTitle: Finite-horizon ${H_{\infty }}$ State Estimation for Discrete-Time Memristive Neural Networks with Time-Varying Delays and Fading Channels: A Dynamic Event-Triggered Approach
abstract: In this paper, we consider the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${H_{\infty }}$</tex> finite-horizon state estimation issue for a class of discrete-time memristive neural networks (DMNNs) with time-varying delays and multiple fading channels. A set of correlated random variables are used to study the correlated fading channels. Specifically, the channel coefficients are assumed to be scalar white noise processes satisfying certain probability distribution laws. At the same time, in order to reduce unnecessary resource consumption in the communication channel between the sensor and remote estimator, a dynamic event-triggered transmission strategy is introduced. Our goal is to construct a set of dynamic event-triggered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${H_{\infty }}$</tex> estimators to ensure that the DMNNs reaches the specified interference attenuation level over a finite time-horizon. With the combination of the Lyapunov-Krasovskii function and stochastic analysis method, sufficient conditions are obtained for the expected estimator. Then, the estimator gains are calculated by solving a set of convex optimization problems. Finally, an example is given to verify the effectiveness and usefulness of the developed state estimation scheme.

articleTitle: Design of target suppression and feature recognition circuit based on memristor
abstract: In the practical application of TV tracking, it is very important to realize the automatic recognition and suppression of the target signal in the field of view. A memristor-based target suppression and feature recognition circuit is proposed in this paper, which uses a simple method to suppress redundant targets and identify targets more accurately. The circuit consists of two selective input modules, two target suppression modules, two feature recognition modules and a signal processing module. The selection input module can realize the selection of multiple features of a single object in the field of view. The designed target suppression module realizes the suppression of redundant interference targets through a simple circuit and reduces the influence of interference signals on the recognition system. According to the characteristic information of the target signal, the feature recognition module finally realizes the recognition of the target signal. The circuit designed in this work can overcome the blindness of the suppression target, improve the accuracy of TV tracking, and provide a reference for TV tracking hardware circuit.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised GAN For Occluded Facial Expression Recognition
abstract: Facial occlusion is an important reason for the accuracy decline of facial emotion recognition in the wild. Nowadays almost all existing occluded facial emotion recognition methods are based on supervised learning. To solve this problem, we propose a generative adversarial network based framework in this paper to perform occluded facial expression recognition in a self-supervised way. The framework is composed of one generator G and three discriminators Do, D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, the generator G is to complete occluded facial part and has an encoder-decoder architecture. Three discriminators have same network structure, the real-fake discriminator D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is to identify whether input image is generated, the mask discriminator D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> is to identify whether occlusion exists in image, the emotion discriminator D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is a classifier which used to output emotion label. Four loss functions are used in training process, which are adversarial loss L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">adv</inf>; pixel loss L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pixel</inf>; mask loss L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mask</inf>and classification loss L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. To verify the effectiveness of this proposed method, experiments are designed on two datasets: CK+ and AffectNet, and we analyze the results of experiments, which proves that the framework this paper proposed can effectively reduce the influence of facial occlusion on emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Improved Neural Network Crawler with Information Entropy and Memristor Model
abstract: This paper presents a framework of Hopfield neural network crawler with information entropy and memristor model to design two novel methods for calculation of the relevance of hypertext link, which optimizes crawling strategy. Based on single-layer Hopfield neural network, adopting breadth-best-first crawling strategy, designing memristor-based activation function, and applying information entropy and cubic nonlinearity memristor model to calculate hyperlink weight are highlighted. Our experimental results on a series of Tibet development topics demonstrate the performance of our crawlers, which efficiently increase the topic-relevant similarity and achieve higher precision than other crawlers.

articleTitle: MC-CapsNet : Low-level Pooling and High-level Fusion of Multi-columns Capsule Network
abstract: Capsule network is a new type of neural network structure. The biggest feature of capsule network is “vector in vector out”, which replaces the previous “scalar in scalar out”. The pristine capsule network completely discards the pooling layers and uses a convolutional kernel size of 9 × 9 to increase the perceptual field However, since the original capsule network has only two feature extraction layers, it cannot extract high level abstract features of objects, which are very important for image classification. Moreover, the original capsule network completely discards the use of pooling layers. Based on the above problems, we propose a multi-column capsule network (MC-CapsNet) with low-level pooling and high-level fusion. Unlike the traditional capsule network, MC-CapsNet has the following features: (a)MC-CapsNet consists of two columns of capsule network: the primary column of capsule network extracts high-level impalpable features; the other column of capsule network extracts subordinate shallow features (b)Pooling operation is added to the initial two convolutional layers of the two columns of capsule network (c)Using the high-level theoretical features extracted from the first capsule network to fuse features with the low-level surface layers extracted from the second capsule network to achieve feature complementarily (d)We add the elements of the digital capsule layers in the two-column capsule network to increase the probability of object features being detected by the capsule. The experimental results show that the classification accuracy of MC-CapsNet reaches 87.96% and 94.42% on the CIFAR10 and FashionMNIST datasets.

articleTitle: TRC-GCN: Two Residual Connections in Graph Convolution Networks for Node Classification Tasks
abstract: Recently, several variants of graph convolution networks (GCNs), which have shown awesome performance in node classification tasks, were investigated. This paper proposes a new GCN model by adding two residual connections (TRC), one is the initial residual connection, and the other is the residual connection to the previous layer. Moreover, a new adjacency matrix and a simpler method for realizing identity mapping are presented and integrated into the TRC-GCN model. The advantage of our TRC-GCN is that the representation of the target node integrates more information, which can learn node embeddings more outstandingly, so as to perform downstream tasks more effectively. Then, we use this model to perform node classification experiments on several datasets (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed), and found that this model is more excellent than many other models.

articleTitle: Exponential Synchronization of Nonlinear Interconnected Reaction-Diffusion Memristive NNs under Stochastic Cyber Attacks via Pointwise Control
abstract: For a class of nonlinear interconnected memristive NNs (IMNNs) with reaction-diffusion terms, the exponential synchronization issue under stochastic cyber attacks is investigated in this article. More specifically, this article considers a special situation that the reaction-diffusion IMNNs is hit by cyber attacks that are governed by a Bernoulli distributed variable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta(t)$</tex>, which influences communication links and causes changes in network topology. Besides, to overcome the shortcomings of the traditional distributed full state feedback control strategies in implementations, this article attempts to employ collocated pointwise control scheme to reduce the control cost and complexity. The Lyapunov theory and Laplacian matrix method are used to derive the exponential synchronization criterion to guarantee that all the subsystems's states are consistent. A numerical experiment demonstrates the efficacy of the designed controller.

articleTitle: Dissipative State Estimation for Delayed Discrete-Time Memristive Neural Networks Under Dynamic Event-Triggered Mechanisms and Deception Attacks
abstract: In this paper, the state estimation problem for delayed discrete-time memristive neural networks subject to deception attacks is concerned. The main purpose is to design a state estimator such that the error dynamics of the state estimation is stochastically stable and strict dissipative. The randomness of deception attacks is described via a set of Bernoulli distributed white sequences with known conditional probabilities. In addition, in order to reduce unnecessary resource consumption in the communication channels, a dynamic event-triggering mechanism is introduced. By using the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional and stochastic analysis method, sufficient conditions for stochastic stability and strict dissipation of the error system are acquired. On this basis, a co-design scheme of estimator parameters and the event-triggered matrix is proposed. Finally, the numerical simulation shows the effectiveness of the proposed state estimation scheme.
